papers.title: Graphene oxide/alginate composites as novel bioinks for three-dimensional mesenchymal stem cell printing and bone regeneration applications.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) cell printing is a versatile technique enabling the creation of 3D constructs containing hydrogel and cells in the desired shape or pattern. Bioinks exhibiting appropriate mechanical properties and biological activities to support cell growth and/or differentiation toward a specific lineage play critical roles in 3D cell printing and tissue engineering applications. Herein, we explored alginate/graphene oxide (GO) composites as bioinks for their potential to improve printability, structural stability, and osteogenic activities for osteogenic tissue engineering applications. The addition of GO (0.05-1.0 mg mL-1) to 3% alginate significantly enhanced the printing performances of the alginate bioink. In addition, mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) printed with alginate/GO showed good proliferation and higher survival in an oxidative stress environment. The 3D scaffolds printed with MSCs and alginate/GO demonstrated significantly enhanced osteogenic differentiation compared with those printed with MSCs and alginate. Overall, a bioink of 3% alginate and 0.5 mg mL-1 GO showed the most balanced characteristics in terms of printability, structural stability, and osteogenic induction of the printed MSCs. Alginate/GO composite bioinks will be useful for bioprinting research for various tissue engineering applications.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及任何人工智能方法，与AI生物打印方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not integrate AI into any bioprinting workflow stage; it is purely a material science study on bioink formulation.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发具有改进机械性能和成骨活性的生物墨水用于骨再生。
summary_zh.method: 将氧化石墨烯加入海藻酸钠中形成复合生物墨水，用于打印间充质干细胞。
summary_zh.result: 添加0.5 mg/mL GO的海藻酸钠生物墨水打印性能最佳，并显著增强成骨分化。
summary_zh.validation: 通过打印性能测试和体外细胞培养验证。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a composite bioink with enhanced printability and osteogenic activity for bone tissue engineering.
summary_en.method: Graphene oxide was incorporated into alginate to formulate composite bioinks for 3D printing of mesenchymal stem cells.
summary_en.result: The alginate/0.5 mg/mL GO bioink exhibited optimal printability and significantly promoted osteogenic differentiation of printed MSCs.
summary_en.validation: Printability was assessed via extrusion testing, and biological performance was validated through in vitro cell culture experiments.
